mainTopic: Whether a small item mixed into someone else's larger item loses its identity (ביטול), and how this affects borrowed water and salt in dough and its תחום on יום טוב
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of why a neighbor's borrowed water and salt are not בטל in a woman's dough, so the dough is limited by the neighbor's תחום too. רבי אבא compared it to one person's קב of wheat mixed into another's ten קבין, but the חכמים laughed at him. רב אושעיא defended them: according to רבנן, even wheat mixed with wheat is בטל. רב ספרא answered with רב's ruling that someone who removes pebbles from a friend's grain pile pays the value of wheat, because removing a mixed-in part lowers the measure. אביי replied that money someone is demanding back is different from property no one is claiming. רב ספרא pushed back with רב חסדא's rule about נבלה and שחוטה and with רבי יוחנן בן נורי's teaching that ownerless objects acquire שביתה. אביי answered that an איסור can be nullified, but money cannot. So the גמרא asks for the real reason. אביי says it is a גזירה because of dough made in partnership, and רבא says salt is added for taste, and taste is never nullified.

steps.title: רבי אבא's wheat comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא argues that a small amount of one person's food mixed into a larger amount of another's does not simply become the second person's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose one person's single קב of wheat got mixed into ten קבין of his friend's wheat. Should the friend just eat all of it and be happy?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is finishing his argument with a sharp example. If a small amount of one person's wheat gets mixed into another's, the small owner doesn't lose his share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that the borrowed water and salt in the dough still belong to the lender, so they are not wiped out by the larger dough. He uses wheat as a clear, everyday case where nobody would say the small owner just loses everything.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of volume (for grain, etc.)

phrases.english: Suppose one's single kav of wheat became mixed
into ten kav of wheat belonging to his fellow,
shall that other one eat it all and rejoice?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אבא's argument from before this section about water and salt in a dough.
steps.raayaObject: That the borrowed water and salt keep their owner's identity and are not בטל in the dough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Common sense: one person's קב of wheat mixed into another's ten קבין does not become the other person's.

steps.title: The חכמים laugh at רבי אבא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים laugh at רבי אבא's example. He protests, and they laugh again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at him. He said to them: Did I take your cloaks? They laughed at him again.
steps.whatsHappening: The listeners reject רבי אבא's comparison by laughing at it. He is offended and asks why they are treating him this way, but they laugh again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laughter shows they thought his comparison was weak, but they do not explain why. The next step, from רב אושעיא, will explain what they were thinking.

phrases.english: They laughed at him.
He said to them: Did I take your cloaks?
phrases.notes: He means: what did I do to you that you're embarrassing me like this?

phrases.english: They laughed at him again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The listeners react to רבי אבא's comparison by rejecting it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated here; רב אושעיא explains it in the next step.

steps.title: רב אושעיא explains why the laughter was right
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא says the חכמים were right: by רבנן, even wheat mixed into wheat is בטל, so רבי אבא's example proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: They did well to laugh at him. Why didn't he use wheat mixed with barley as his example? Because that is one kind mixed with a different kind, and a different kind is בטל. But wheat mixed with wheat is also like that: even though by רבי יהודה it is not בטל, by רבנן it certainly is בטל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא defends the people who laughed. He shows that רבי אבא's wheat example doesn't work according to רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא chose wheat-in-wheat because he knew that a different kind (מין בשאינו מינו) is clearly בטל. But רב אושעיא points out that only רבי יהודה says same-kind (מין במינו) is not בטל; רבנן say it is בטל too. So by רבנן, the friend really could keep all the wheat, and the example fails.

keyTerms.meaning: One kind mixed with a different kind
Becomes cancelled out, loses its identity in the mixture

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא picked wheat-in-wheat on purpose, because he thought same-kind is not בטל. רב אושעיא is not saying he forgot about barley; he is saying the wheat case also doesn't help him, since רבנן say same-kind is בטל too.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
They did well to laugh at him.
What is different about wheat mixed with barley
that he did not say that case to them?
Because that is one kind mixed with a different kind,
and one kind mixed with a different kind is nullified.
Wheat mixed with wheat as well:
granted that according to Rabbi Yehuda it is not nullified,
according to the Rabbis it is certainly nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: שַׁפִּיר עֲבוּד דְּאַחִיכוּ עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the laughter in step 2, defending the חכמים against רבי אבא's challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the challenge's example only works according to one opinion (רבי יהודה), not according to רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא assumed that wheat-in-wheat clearly keeps its owner's identity.
steps.terutzMaskana: By רבנן, same-kind mixtures are also בטל, so the small owner's wheat really is cancelled out.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The analogy only works according to רבי יהודה. According to רבנן, מין במינו is also בטל, so the friend really could keep all the wheat.

steps.title: רב ספרא challenges רב אושעיא with the pebbles case
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא questions רב אושעיא's defense, citing רב's ruling that one who removes pebbles from a friend's grain pile must pay the price of wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to him: משה! Did you speak well?! Didn't they hear what רבי חייא קטוספאה said in the name of רב: Someone who removes pebbles from his friend's grain pile must pay him the value of wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא pushes back on רב אושעיא. He brings a teaching of רב that seems to show a small mixed-in amount is not simply ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pebbles are mixed into the wheat and are worthless by themselves, yet removing them costs the owner money, so he must be paid as if for wheat. That suggests the mixed-in pebbles were not just 'gone' inside the wheat. This attacks רב אושעיא's claim that the small amount is simply בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'משה!' — a respectful way of addressing a great scholar

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to him: Moses!
phrases.notes: Calling him משה is a way of showing great respect, like calling him the leader of the generation.

phrases.english: Have you spoken well?!
But did they not hear this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא קְטוֹסְפָאָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Chiyya of Ketosfa'a said in the name of Rav:
One who removes pebbles from his fellow's grain pile
is obligated to pay him the value of wheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא: מֹשֶׁה! שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אושעיא's defense of the laughter in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אושעיא's claim that the small mixed-in amount is simply בטל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that even worthless pebbles mixed into wheat count, since removing them costs the owner money; so a mixed-in amount is not ignored.

steps.title: Removing it lowers the measure
steps.stepSummary: From רב's ruling we learn that taking out a mixed-in amount lowers the measure, and the same applies to the water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that he lowered his measure. Here too, he lowered his measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא draws the lesson from the pebbles case and applies it back to our case of the borrowed water and salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pebbles were sold as part of the wheat's measure, so removing them took away real value. In the same way, the water and salt are a real part of the dough's amount, so they are not cancelled out. This supports רבי אבא and shows the laughter was not justified.

keyTerms.meaning: He lowered it, made it less

steps.whatToRemember: רב אושעיא defended the laughter, saying רבנן hold same-kind mixtures are בטל. רב ספרא answered with רב's pebbles ruling: a mixed-in part still counts because removing it lowers the measure, so he argues the water and salt in the dough are not cancelled out. אביי will challenge this proof next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רב ספרא's attempt to back up רבי אבא's point that the borrowed water and salt keep their own identity. אביי disputes it in the next steps, and the גמרא ends up giving different reasons (steps 12–13).

phrases.english: Apparently: he reduced his measure.
Here too, he reduced his measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the pebbles source in step 4 and applies it to the dough case.
steps.raayaObject: That the borrowed water and salt are not בטל in the dough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that one who removes pebbles from a friend's grain pile pays the value of wheat.

steps.title: אביי distinguishes property with claimants from property without
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רב's pebbles case is no proof. There the owner demands payment, while the water and salt have no one claiming them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Doesn't the master see a difference between property that someone is demanding back and property that no one is demanding back?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב ספרא's proof from step 5. He says the pebbles case and the water-and-salt case are not the same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's case, the owner of the grain pile wants to be paid, so his share does not disappear. The water and salt were lent and no one is asking for them now, so they might really be בטל in the dough. So the proof from רב does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference, to distinguish
The master, a polite way of saying 'you'

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב ספרא, who brought the proof from רב's pebbles case.

phrases.english: And does the master not distinguish
between property that has claimants
and property that has no claimants?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 5 by drawing a distinction between the two cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's comparison of the water and salt to רב's pebbles ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Property with active claimants keeps its identity. Property with no one claiming it may be nullified, so the comparison fails.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ספרא's proof (steps 4-5) from רב's pebbles ruling to the borrowed water and salt.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pebbles belong to an owner who is demanding payment. The lent water and salt have no one claiming them, so they may be בטל.

steps.title: רב ספרא cites רב חסדא on carcass meat mixed with slaughtered meat
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא responds 'by your logic' and brings רב חסדא's rule. A נבלה is nullified in שחוטה, but שחוטה is not nullified in נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By your reasoning, consider what רב חסדא said. Carcass meat is nullified in slaughtered meat, because slaughtered meat can never become a carcass. Slaughtered meat is not nullified in carcass meat, because a carcass can become like slaughtered meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא begins his answer to אביי by quoting a rule from רב חסדא. This step sets up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule decides nullification by whether one meat can turn into the other kind. Nothing in the rule depends on who owns the meat. רב ספרא is about to use that fact against אביי's distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, a 'by your logic' challenge
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Meat of a properly slaughtered animal
Is nullified, absorbed into the majority

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
that which Rav Chisda said:
Carcass meat is nullified in slaughtered meat,
because it is impossible for slaughtered meat
to become carcass meat.
Slaughtered meat is not nullified in carcass meat,
because it is possible for carcass meat
to become like slaughtered meat.
phrases.notes: If a נבלה rots until it isn't fit to eat, it stops making things טמא, just like שחוטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רב ספרא's counter-attack on אביי's distinction by bringing an outside ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nullification depends on whether one item can take on the other's status, not on ownership.

steps.title: Would ownership really stop the carcass from being nullified?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks whether, by אביי's logic, a נבלה that has an owner would not be nullified. That would be a strange result.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would you say here too that when the carcass has owners, it is not nullified?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא now makes his challenge. If owners matter, אביי would have to say that a נבלה belonging to someone is not בטל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule clearly does not depend on whether the meat has an owner. If אביי's distinction were right, ownership would suddenly change the law of nullification. רב ספרא presents this as hard to accept.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכִי אִית לַהּ בְּעָלִים
phrases.english: Would you say here too that when it has owners
it is not nullified?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכִי אִית לַהּ בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies אביי's distinction to רב חסדא's ruling to show where it leads.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's distinction between property with claimants and property without
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ownership mattered, a נבלה with an owner would not be nullified. Nobody suggests that in רב חסדא's rule.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: ownerless objects are treated like owned objects
steps.stepSummary: Suppose אביי accepts that ownership matters. רב ספרא then cites רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who teaches that ownerless objects acquire שביתה as if they had owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say yes, that is so, isn't it taught: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said that ownerless objects acquire a שבת resting place. Even though they have no owners, they are treated as if they have owners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא blocks אביי's way out. He brings a ברייתא showing that, for שביתה, things without owners are treated the same as things with owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed that property with no claimants might lose its own status. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says that even ownerless things have their own שבת place, as if someone owned them. So having or not having a claimant does not change the תחום, and the water and salt keep their own limits.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא
Acquire a שבת resting place, which sets their תחום

steps.whatToRemember: רב ספרא attacks אביי's distinction twice. He argues that nullification does not depend on owners (רב חסדא), and that for תחום, ownerless things count as if they had owners (רבי יוחנן בן נורי). אביי answers in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you say: indeed, that is so,
but isn't it taught:
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
Ownerless objects acquire a Shabbos resting place.
phrases.notes: Wherever they sit when שבת starts becomes their base, so they can only be moved within the תחום from there.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם בְּעָלִים
phrases.english: Even though they have no owners,
they are treated as if they have owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the possible reply to step 8 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That lacking a claimant or owner does not cancel an object's own תחום status
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוחנן בן נורי: חפצי הפקר קונין שביתה
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's distinction between property with claimants and property without, if he accepts that an owned נבלה is not בטל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן בן נורי teaches that ownerless objects are treated as if they have owners for שביתה. So lacking an owner or claimant does not erase an object's own status.

steps.title: אביי answers that prohibitions and money work differently
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רב ספרא: a case of איסור cannot be compared to a case of ממון. An איסור can be nullified, but money cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב ספרא: Are you comparing a prohibition to money? A prohibition can be nullified. Money cannot be nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב ספרא's attack. He explains that the נבלה case is about איסור, while רב's pebbles case is about money, so they follow different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא tried to show that ownership cannot be what matters, since a נבלה with an owner is still nullified. אביי answers that ownership matters only in money cases. A forbidden food gets ביטול no matter who owns it, but a person's money never just disappears into someone else's. So the pebbles case still cannot prove anything about the water and salt.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition (a matter of ritual law)
Money, a matter of who owns what
Becomes nullified, cancelled out in a larger mixture

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the water and salt are a money case. He is saying רב's pebbles were a money case, so they cannot serve as proof for an איסור case.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are you comparing
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רב ספרא.

phrases.english: a prohibition to money?
A prohibition is nullified,
money is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי rejects רב ספרא's challenge by separating איסור rules from ממון rules.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ספרא's use of the נבלה case to argue against אביי's ownership distinction.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ספרא mixed a money case with an איסור case. Ownership matters for money but not for ביטול of איסור.

steps.title: So why aren't the water and salt nullified?
steps.stepSummary: Since an איסור can normally be nullified, the גמרא asks for the real reason the water and salt are not nullified in the dough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its original question and asks for the real reason. This short line sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי just said that an איסור is normally nullified. The water and salt carry an איסור of תחום, and they are only a small part of the dough. So by the normal rule they should be nullified, and the משנה's ruling needs a reason.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why don't the neighbor's water and salt get nullified in the dough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because איסור is normally nullified (step 10), the original question about the משנה comes back.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the small amount of water and salt does not become nullified in the dough, even though they carry an איסור of תחום.

steps.title: אביי: a decree because of dough made in partnership
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the rule is a rabbinic גזירה. We worry that people would confuse this case with dough made in partnership.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a decree, in case a woman makes dough in partnership.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his reason. Strictly speaking, the water and salt should be nullified, but the חכמים made a גזירה anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When neighbors make dough together as partners, the dough truly belongs to all of them and is limited by everyone's תחום. A small borrowed amount looks similar to partnership dough. So the חכמים treated both cases the same, so that people would not get confused.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is a decree
lest she make dough in partnership.
phrases.notes: Partnership dough really belongs to everyone, so the חכמים didn't want people mixing up the two cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא תַּעֲשֶׂה עִיסָּה בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The water and salt are not nullified because of a rabbinic גזירה, so that borrowed ingredients are not confused with dough made in partnership.

steps.title: רבא: spices give taste, and taste is never nullified
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason. A spice like salt is added for its taste, and taste does not get nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Spices are made for taste, and taste is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, separate answer to the same question. He says there is no ביטול here at all, so no גזירה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביטול works when a small ingredient gets lost and doesn't matter. Salt is added to the dough so that people will taste it. Since its effect is meant to be felt, it is not treated as lost, so it does not become nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: Taste (the same word as 'reason' in step 11)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons the neighbor's ingredients are not nullified. אביי says it is a rabbinic גזירה because of partnership dough. רבא says a spice gives taste, and taste is not nullified.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's rule that taste is never nullified is a principle used in many places, not only in the laws of תחום.

phrases.english: Rava said: Spices are made for taste,
and taste is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 11 that disagrees with אביי's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Salt is a spice added for taste, and since taste is never nullified, the salt keeps its own status in the dough.
